_doc: HMTc Category 8 (Water and Water-Based Products) compiler config. Method v2.0, government-limit-only. This is the most comprehensively regulated category in the HMTc taxonomy: nine of the eleven panel cells carry a number on every row (eight direct sovereign maxima plus a disclosed read-across on the mineral-water row, where aluminium is the one cell no government sets for natural mineral water; nine direct sovereign maxima on the other three rows), because two whole instrument families reach the product form — national drinking-water regulations (US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations as incorporated by FDA, EU Directive 2020/2184, Health Canada GDWQ, NHMRC ADWG, California SWRCB Title 22, WHO GDWQ) and the packaged-water lines of national food-contaminant schedules (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, India FSSAI 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013, Chile Decreto 977/1996, Fiji FSR 2009). Every number is a named register id; none is occurrence-derived. Two cells carry no number on any row and are handled honestly rather than invented: tin, for which no government sets a water maximum and for which the only near-neighbour (canned-beverage tinplate migration at 100 mg/kg) is four orders of magnitude out of range, is a CONTROL; methylmercury, which no government regulates in water and which is bounded by identity under the published total-mercury ceiling, is NOT-MATERIAL on the speciation-bounded basis class. Two deliberate departures from HMTc defaults are documented in _category.method_note and in the affected cells' substantiation: total chromium is published as a FIRM limit rather than a screen (the drinking-water instruments regulate the total because the species interconvert in water, and Health Canada says so in terms), and the credible-regulator set is widened to the authorities that actually publish a packaged-water metals line so the stricter-unselected audit scans the complete instrument pool. TWO CELLS ARE READ-ACROSS ON EVERY ROW BECAUSE THEIR ANCHOR'S SCOPE IS DRINKING-WATER SUPPLY RATHER THAN PACKAGED PRODUCT, and the hop is on the face of the record rather than buried in prose: hexavalent chromium at 10 µg/L (California Title 22 s.64431, product scope 'public water systems in California'; the exact packaged-water cell is unregulated worldwide) and cadmium at 2 µg/L (NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines, a non-statutory guideline for drinking-water supplies; Australia regulates packaged water under the FSANZ Food Standards Code, whose packaged-water metals cell is absent from the register). Neither value changed when the tag was corrected; both remain the strictest applicable figure and both run in the protective direction. KNOWN POOL GAP: Commission Directive 2003/40/EC, the EU metals instrument for natural mineral waters, is absent from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv and therefore from every mineral-water candidate set; it is disclosed at row level and on the affected cells, and no numeric value is asserted for it. Allowed provenance tags: regulatory-alignment, read-across, not-material, control, ratchet. STAFF / HMTc content, not public wiki (CLAUDE.md Part 19 firewall). CHANGE LOG. v1.1 (2026-08-17), adversarial-audit remediation, no published value moved: cadmium and hexavalent chromium retagged from regulatory-alignment to disclosed read-across on all four rows because their anchors scope to drinking-water supply rather than packaged product, with the scope hop now visible in each record as source_scope; the category method note corrected, since the 50-versus-25 total-chromium difference is a consequence of the Directive 2020/2184 natural-mineral-water scope exclusion and NOT an instrument-written split (Hong Kong Cap 132V writes 50 ug/L for both packaged-water forms), and the one genuine instrument-written split in the pool is Hong Kong nickel; the packaged-water bridge restated as a checkable test with the two cells that fail it named and the one open EU scope-pinpoint verification item recorded; Commission Directive 2003/40/EC disclosed as a register gap at row level and on every affected mineral-water cell, and the unbacked 50 ug/L figure previously asserted for it removed; the four MeHg not-material determinations confirmed present in data/evidence/standards-not-material.csv and passing the build-blocking substantiation gate.

_category.name: Water and Water-Based Products
_category.anchor: strictest applicable sovereign drinking-water or packaged-water maximum, per litre of finished product as consumed, with natural mineral water kept as the separate product form the instruments themselves treat it as (Hong Kong Cap 132V writes dedicated natural-mineral-water lines; EU Directive 2020/2184 excludes the form from its scope)
_category.basis_family: dietary as-consumed, per litre of finished packaged water (µg/L, numerically interchangeable with µg/kg at unit density)
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; strictest applicable sovereign maximum for the exact packaged-water form in its native per-litre as-consumed basis, disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, control where no defensible sovereign number exists; never occurrence-derived)
_category.method_note: Two applicability rules govern every row in this category and are applied uniformly. (1) THE PACKAGED-WATER BRIDGE. A national drinking-water maximum is treated as directly applicable to a packaged-water row because the product is the same substance assessed in the same basis (µg per litre of water as consumed), and because the two largest jurisdictions write that bridge into their own packaged-water rules: the FDA bottled-water standard of quality incorporates the EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulation maximum contaminant levels by reference at 21 CFR 165.110(b)(4)(iii), and the scope of EU Directive 2020/2184 expressly reaches water put into bottles or containers. The bridge is disclosed, not silent, and it is never applied where the instrument itself carves the product form out. THE TEST THE BRIDGE APPLIES, stated so that it can be checked rather than assumed: a national drinking-water maximum is tagged regulatory-alignment on a packaged-water row ONLY where that instrument's own text reaches packaged product (EU Directive 2020/2184, whose scope definition of water intended for human consumption extends to water put into bottles or containers; FDA 21 CFR 165.110(b)(4)(iii), which incorporates the EPA maximum contaminant levels into the bottled-water standard of quality). Where an instrument's scope is drinking-water SUPPLY and no such text reaches packaged product, its value is carried as a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS instead, never as an asserted maximum for the packaged form. Two cells in this category fail the test and are read-across on every row for exactly that reason: cadmium, whose 2 µg/L anchor is a non-statutory NHMRC guideline for Australian drinking-water supplies while Australia regulates packaged water under the FSANZ Food Standards Code; and hexavalent chromium, whose 10 µg/L anchor is a California Title 22 maximum contaminant level whose register scope is 'public water systems in California'. Neither value changed when its tag was corrected. ONE VERIFICATION ITEM IS OPEN AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the register's product_scope field for the EU rows reads 'water intended for human consumption' and does not itself record the packaged-water reach, so the EU half of the bridge rests on the Directive's scope definition rather than on anything visible in the register row. The pinpoint article and clause should be captured into the register's notes at the next regulatory-fetch pass; the exposure is bounded and is stated exactly. On the three non-mineral rows, lead (5 µg/L), total arsenic (10 µg/L), total mercury (1 µg/L) and aluminium (200 µg/L) are each independently matched at the same figure by an instrument that is packaged-scoped on its face or reaches bottled water through the FDA incorporation, so those cells do not depend on the EU bridge at all. TWO CELLS DO DEPEND ON IT ALONE: total chromium at 25 µg/L, where the next tier is 50 µg/L, and nickel at 20 µg/L, where the nearest packaged-scoped value for this exact form is Hong Kong's 70 µg/L for bottled or packaged drinking waters other than natural mineral waters and the only other 20 µg/L values are Hong Kong's natural-mineral-water line (a different product form) and the NHMRC guideline (the same supply-scope limitation). If the EU scope pinpoint does not survive verification, those two cells convert to disclosed read-across on the same value rather than moving, and that is recorded here in advance so the conversion is a documented step and not a discovery. (2) THE NATURAL-MINERAL-WATER CARVE-OUT. Directive 2020/2184 excludes natural mineral waters recognised under Directive 2009/54/EC, so no Drinking Water Directive value is used on the mineral-water row. The EU instrument that does set metals limits for natural mineral waters is Commission Directive 2003/40/EC (2009/54/EC defines the product but sets no metals values); it is ABSENT from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, is therefore absent from the candidate set of every cell on the mineral-water row, and is logged as a register gap to be retrieved through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway. No numeric value is asserted for it anywhere in this standard, because every number here traces to a named register row and an instrument that is not in the register supplies none; the mineral-water row is recompiled against it when it lands. FDA exempts mineral water from its aesthetically based (secondary) allowable levels, which is why the mineral-water aluminium cell is a disclosed read-across rather than a direct government limit. The 50-versus-25 total-chromium difference between the mineral-water row and the other three rows is NOT an instrument-written split, and is not presented as one. Hong Kong Cap 132V writes 50 µg/L for BOTH packaged-water forms (hk_cap132v_crtotal_natural-mineral-waters_50 and hk_cap132v_crtotal_bottled-or-packaged-drinking-waters-other-than-natural_50), and Health Canada, WHO and California each write a single unsplit chromium value of 50 µg/L; no instrument in this pool writes a 50-versus-25 chromium split. The difference is a consequence of SCOPE alone: because Directive 2020/2184 excludes natural mineral water, the Directive's 25 µg/L end-state chromium value is not an applicable maximum for the mineral-water row, which therefore takes the Hong Kong Cap 132V natural-mineral-waters value of 50 µg/L, while the other three rows take the applicable Directive value of 25 µg/L. The one genuine instrument-written product-form split in this category's pool is Hong Kong's nickel line, 20 µg/L for natural mineral waters against 70 µg/L for other packaged drinking waters; it is honoured in the anchor selection on the mineral-water row, but it produces no published difference between rows because EU Directive 2020/2184 independently puts the other three rows at 20 µg/L. Where an instrument does write a product-form split HMTc preserves it rather than smoothing it away, and where none exists HMTc does not manufacture one. UNIT BASIS. Every value is expressed per litre of finished packaged product as consumed. Instruments stating mg/kg (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011) and instruments stating mg/L are compared at face value because the density of potable water is within 0.3 per cent of 1 kg/L across the packaging and storage range, so µg/kg and µg/L are the same number to well inside analytical uncertainty. No reconstitution or dilution conversion is applied anywhere in this category; the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula and is expressly not used on the infant nursery-water row. TOTAL CHROMIUM IS FIRM, NOT A SCREEN. In a food matrix total chromium is dominated by nutritionally benign Cr(III) and is a poor proxy for the health-relevant species, which is why HMTc normally records it as a screen. Water is the documented exception: the drinking-water instruments regulate total chromium precisely because the two species interconvert in aqueous media, and the Health Canada entry states that the maximum acceptable concentration protects against chromium(VI) effects and is established for total chromium. Hexavalent chromium is additionally published as its own cell, so the species control is not displaced by the total. NON-HEALTH-BASED AND FUTURE-DATED ANCHORS ARE LABELLED. Aluminium at 200 µg/L is an EU Annex I Part C indicator parameter, an FDA secondary (aesthetic) allowable level and an NHMRC aesthetic guideline, and is presented as such rather than as a toxicological line. The EU lead (5 µg/L) and total-chromium (25 µg/L) parametric values are the Directive's end-state values, which member states must meet by 12 January 2036 and below which transitional values of 10 and 50 µg/L apply until then; HMTc adopts the end-state values now, so those cells are stricter than currently-enforced EU practice, which is disclosed rather than presented as current EU law. For lead the number is independently compelled by the in-force FDA allowable level of 5 µg/L.
_category.credible_note: Category 8 is governed by two instrument families: national drinking-water regulations and the packaged-water lines of national food-contaminant schedules. The default credible set (EU, UK, Codex, international, US, AU-NZ, CA, HK) omits most of the authorities that actually publish a packaged-water metals line, which would leave the stricter-unselected audit scanning only a fraction of the applicable pool and would risk exactly the missed-stricter-anchor failure the audit exists to catch. The set is therefore widened to every jurisdiction in the register that publishes a drinking-water or packaged-water maximum for a panel analyte: AU (NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines), US-CA (California State Water Resources Control Board Title 22 section 64431 inorganic-chemical MCLs, the only enforceable hexavalent-chromium drinking-water maximum anywhere in the register), WHO (Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality), IL, IN, VN, GSO, CO, CL and FJ. Admission to the scan pool is not endorsement and does not by itself make a value binding: a row binds only where it is applicable to the exact product form AND is the strictest such value, and the widening is what makes the audit's silence meaningful. WHO guideline values are advisory rather than national law (the register records this on the rows themselves) and are carried for corroboration and audit completeness; no published value in this category rests on a WHO guideline value as its binding source. California is a sub-national government and its selection on the hexavalent-chromium cell is disclosed as such in that cell's substantiation.

bottled-drinking-water.name: Bottled drinking water (purified, spring, artesian)
bottled-drinking-water.native_basis_label: as consumed, per litre of finished bottled water (µg/L; numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
bottled-drinking-water.scope_note: This row is packaged water as placed on the market and assessed per litre as consumed. It is governed by the packaged-water bridge stated in the category method note: national drinking-water maxima apply because the product is the same substance in the same basis, and because FDA incorporates the EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulation MCLs into the bottled-water standard of quality at 21 CFR 165.110(b)(4)(iii) while the scope of EU Directive 2020/2184 expressly reaches water put into bottles or containers. In scope: purified, distilled, deionised, reverse-osmosis, spring, artesian and well water sold packaged for drinking, unflavoured and unsweetened, in any container. Out of scope: natural mineral water, which is a legally distinct product form with its own row and its own instrument (EU Directive 2009/54/EC and Commission Directive 2003/40/EC; the Hong Kong Cap 132V line for this row reads 'bottled or packaged drinking waters, OTHER THAN natural mineral waters'); unflavoured carbonated water, which has its own row; and any flavoured, sweetened, mineral-fortified, vitamin-added or functional water, which routes to HMTc Category 5 (Beverages) by the Category 8 boundary rule because flavouring changes both the matrix and the regulatory treatment. Water sold for formula preparation routes to the infant nursery-water row.
bottled-drinking-water.cross_reference: Flavoured, sweetened or functional waters route to HMTc Category 5 (Beverages). Natural mineral water is the mineral-water row of this category.

bottled-drinking-water.basis_guard: ^(?!.*(dry weight|dry matter|dehydrated|migration|leach|material content|surface|\bfeed\b|fat basis))(?=.*(water|as[ _]?consumed|mg/l|placed on market|food as listed)).*$
bottled-drinking-water.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a dietary per-litre / as-consumed water or food-schedule basis. The guard rejects dry-weight, dehydrated, migration/leachate, article material-content and feed bases outright, so a dry-commodity maximum level or a food-contact migration limit can never anchor a per-litre water cell. It admits mg/kg-expressed food-schedule rows (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011) because potable water density is within 0.3 per cent of 1 kg/L, so µg/kg and µg/L are the same number to well inside analytical uncertainty; that is a stated identity, not a silent conversion.

Pb.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum for packaged drinking water (EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B end-state value; matched by FDA 21 CFR 165.110, Health Canada and NHMRC)
Pb.basis_label: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Pb.substantiation: Lead at 5 µg/L is the strictest applicable sovereign maximum and it is corroborated four ways: the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B parametric value, the FDA bottled-water allowable level at 21 CFR 165.110 (0.005 mg/L), the Health Canada maximum acceptable concentration and the NHMRC health-based guideline value. The Directive's 5 µg/L is its end-state value, which member states must meet by 12 January 2036 and below which the transitional value of 10 µg/L applies until then; HMTc adopts the end-state value now, so this cell is stricter than currently-enforced EU practice, but the FDA value of 5 µg/L is in force today and is independently sufficient to compel the number. The looser 10 µg/L values (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, the WHO provisional guideline value, and the Codex/mineral-water family) are named in the candidate set and are not selected because the method takes the strictest applicable value.

read_across.label: disclosed read-across from the NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines health-based guideline value; the ADWG governs drinking-water supplies rather than packaged product, and Australia's packaged-water cadmium cell is absent from the register
read_across.substantiation: Cadmium at 2 µg/L is the NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines health-based guideline value (0.002 mg/L, nhmrc2025_cd_drinking_water_2), the strictest cadmium value any government sets for water. It is published as a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS and not as a direct maximum for this product form, and the reason is stated rather than left to inference. The register records that instrument's product scope as 'drinking water' and its note describes it as a health-based guideline value; the Australian Drinking Water Guidelines are a non-statutory guideline for drinking-water supplies, and Australia regulates packaged water not under the ADWG but under the FSANZ Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code. No FSANZ packaged-water metals row exists in the register: of the AU, NZ and AU-NZ rows, the only water-scoped entries are the eight NHMRC drinking-water guideline values, and Schedule 19 is represented only by commodity rows (formula, cereals, fish, salt and the like). The Australian packaged-water cadmium cell is therefore absent from the register and is logged as a register gap, in the same way Commission Directive 2003/40/EC is logged on the mineral-water row. The category's two textual packaged-water bridges do not carry this instrument either: FDA 21 CFR 165.110(b)(4)(iii) incorporates the EPA maximum contaminant levels (cadmium 5 µg/L) and EU Directive 2020/2184's scope reaches water put into bottles or containers (cadmium 5 µg/L), and neither reaches an Australian guideline. Absence of a packaged-product carve-out is not affirmative scope, so the earlier regulatory-alignment tag overstated what this instrument does. WHAT THE INSTRUMENTS SET FOR THE EXACT CELL IS STATED OPENLY, because the read-across runs in the protective direction and nothing is served by concealing it: the strictest maximum level any government sets for cadmium in this exact packaged-water form is 3 µg/L, then 5 µg/L (EU Drinking Water Directive eu20202184_cd_drinking_water_5, FDA 21 CFR 165.110 fda21cfr165110_cd_bottled_water_5, EPA MCL epa2018_cd_drinking_water_5, California us_ca_swrcb_2024_cd_cadmium_mcl_5ugl), then 7 µg/L (Health Canada healthcanada2025_cd_drinking_water_7). HMTc publishes the stricter 2 µg/L: the substance and the basis are identical, HMTc does not relax a published limit toward a looser instrument, and the value is unchanged from the earlier compilation. Only the provenance tag is corrected, from regulatory-alignment to read-across, so that the record never claims a sovereign packaged-water maximum that no sovereign has written. The 3 µg/L tier for this exact form is Hong Kong Cap 132V (hk_cap132v_cd_bottled-or-packaged-drinking-waters-other-than-natural_3), Israel FCS 2016 (il_fcs2016_cd_17_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_3) and Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011 (vn_qcvn8_2_2011_cd_bottled-water_3), with the WHO guideline value (who2022_cd_drinking_water_3) at the same figure.

Cd.basis_label: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)

tAs.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum; unanimous at 10 µg/L across the applicable instrument pool
tAs.basis_label: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
tAs.substantiation: Total arsenic at 10 µg/L is unanimous across every applicable instrument in the pool: EU Drinking Water Directive, FDA 21 CFR 165.110, the EPA MCL adopted into the bottled-water standard of quality by reference, California, Health Canada, NHMRC, Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011 and the WHO provisional guideline value. There is no stricter sovereign total-arsenic value for water anywhere in the register. Total arsenic is published as its own cell and is not satisfied by the inorganic-arsenic cell.

iAs.basis_label: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
iAs.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum for the exact product form (Israel FCS 2016 row 16.1, bottled drinking water and mineral water)

tHg.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum (EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B; matched by NHMRC, Health Canada and Israel FCS 2016)
tHg.basis_label: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
tHg.substantiation: Total mercury at 1 µg/L is the strictest applicable sovereign maximum, set independently by the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B, the NHMRC health-based guideline, the Health Canada maximum acceptable concentration (which the source table states applies to all forms of mercury) and the Israel FCS 2016 packaged-water line. The FDA bottled-water allowable level and the California MCL are 2 µg/L and the Vietnamese bottled-water value is 6 µg/L; all are named and none is selected. Total mercury is published as a total and is never satisfied by a methylmercury or inorganic-mercury result.

not_material.rationale: Mercury in sealed packaged drinking water is present essentially as inorganic Hg(II). Methylation is a microbial process requiring anaerobic sulfate- or iron-reducing activity in sediment or biota; it does not occur in a treated, filtered, disinfected and sealed packaged-water matrix, and there is no aquatic food chain in the product to bioaccumulate methylmercury. Methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury, so it is bounded by identity at the published total-mercury ceiling of 1 µg/L. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
not_material.reference_method: Methylmercury is not separately quantified as a routine cell. Total mercury is measured on every certification lot by cold-vapour atomic fluorescence or ICP-MS against the published total-mercury ceiling. Where a lot result reaches or exceeds half the total-mercury ceiling, speciation by GC-ICP-MS or HPLC-ICP-MS is run as a reflex and the source water is investigated; a detectable methyl fraction is an immediate non-conformance regardless of the total-mercury result.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction in the register sets a methylmercury maximum for drinking water, bottled water or natural mineral water: of the 27 methylmercury rows in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, every one is a fish or aquatic-animal tissue limit and none is water-scoped. Every drinking-water and packaged-water instrument in the pool regulates mercury as total mercury with no methyl line, and Hong Kong Cap 132V regulates the packaged-drinking-water mercury cell as INORGANIC mercury (0.006 mg/kg, hk_cap132v_ihg_bottled-or-packaged-drinking-waters-other-than-natural_6), which is direct sovereign confirmation that the regulated mercury species in packaged water is the inorganic one. The only methylmercury maxima anywhere in the register are fish and aquatic-animal limits (for example fda_cpg540600_mehg_fish_1000), which govern a bioaccumulating tissue matrix and have no application to water.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I; EU Commission Directive 2003/40/EC (natural mineral waters — ABSENT from the register and logged as a register gap; this determination does not rest on it, and it is re-tested when the instrument is ingested); US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations; US FDA 21 CFR 165.110; California SWRCB Title 22 s.64431; Health Canada Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality (2025 summary tables); NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines; WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality; Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2; Israel FCS 2016; India FSSAI 2016; Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011; GSO 193/2021; Colombia Res 4506/2013; Chile Decreto 977/1996; Fiji FSR 2009.

Ni.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum (EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B; matched by NHMRC)
Ni.basis_label: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Ni.substantiation: Nickel at 20 µg/L is the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B parametric value, matched exactly by the NHMRC health-based guideline and by the Hong Kong Cap 132V natural-mineral-waters line. The looser candidates are Hong Kong's 70 µg/L for other packaged drinking waters, the WHO guideline value of 70 µg/L, and 100 µg/L from FDA 21 CFR 165.110 and California; all are named and none is selected. The FDA and California nickel values descend from an EPA nickel MCL that was remanded in 1995, which is a further reason not to treat 100 µg/L as the operative ceiling when a current statutory value of 20 µg/L is applicable.

control.rationale: No sovereign sets a tin maximum for drinking water, bottled water or natural mineral water. The drinking-water instrument family carries no tin parameter at all (EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I Parts B and C; US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations; US FDA 21 CFR 165.110 standards of quality; Health Canada; NHMRC; WHO), and none of the national food-schedule packaged-water lines (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, India FSSAI 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013, Chile Decreto 977/1996, Fiji FSR 2009) carries a tin entry for water. A read-across is not supportable: the nearest sovereign tin maxima are the canned-food and canned-beverage maximum levels, which exist to bound dissolution of tin from a tinplate container wall into an acidic canned matrix, and the canned-beverage value (100 mg/kg inorganic tin) sits roughly four orders of magnitude above anything a packaged water can plausibly contain, so importing it would publish a ceiling that functions as no limit at all. The dominant packaging for this category (PET, HDPE, glass, aluminium) contains no tin. Still bottled water is occasionally presented in aluminium or tin-free steel cans, neither of which is a tin source. Tin therefore remains a mandatory control cell; no number is invented.
control.reference_method: Tin by ICP-MS on the finished packaged product in its native per-litre as-consumed basis, on every certification lot, reported against the method limit of quantification rather than a ceiling. Any quantifiable tin result triggers investigation of the container, closure and liner, the filling line and the source water, and lot release is withheld pending root-cause identification and a clean re-test. Where the product is presented in a tinplate or tin-coated container, the EU canned-beverage inorganic-tin maximum level recorded as the companion instrument applies as a regulatory hard stop in addition to this control.

Al.label: strictest applicable sovereign value; an indicator / secondary / aesthetic parameter, disclosed as such
Al.basis_label: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Al.substantiation: Aluminium at 200 µg/L is the strictest applicable sovereign value and is disclosed here as a non-health-based parameter rather than a toxicological line: it is an Annex I Part C INDICATOR parameter in the EU Drinking Water Directive, a SECONDARY (aesthetically based) allowable level at FDA 21 CFR 165.110, and an AESTHETIC guideline for acid-soluble aluminium in the NHMRC guidelines. The health-based alternatives are far looser (Health Canada's maximum acceptable concentration of 2900 µg/L; California's MCL of 1000 µg/L), so adopting 200 µg/L is the strictest applicable treatment and is materially protective. Its aesthetic derivation is stated rather than concealed because the label of the parameter, not only its number, is part of the provenance.

Cr.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum (EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B end-state value)
Cr.basis_label: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Cr.substantiation: Total chromium at 25 µg/L is the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B parametric value, the strictest applicable sovereign maximum; it is the Directive's end-state value, to be met by 12 January 2036, with a transitional value of 50 µg/L in force until then. The 50 µg/L tier (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Health Canada, WHO, California) and the 100 µg/L tier (EPA MCL, FDA 21 CFR 165.110) are named and not selected. This cell is published as a FIRM limit rather than as a screen, which is a deliberate departure from the HMTc default for total chromium and is compelled by the instruments themselves: in a food matrix total chromium is dominated by nutritionally benign Cr(III) and is a poor proxy for the health-relevant species, but the drinking-water instruments regulate total chromium precisely because the two species interconvert in aqueous media, and the Health Canada entry states in terms that the maximum acceptable concentration protects against chromium(VI) effects and is established for total chromium. The hexavalent species is not displaced: it is published separately at 10 µg/L.

read_across.label: disclosed read-across from the California SWRCB Title 22 s.64431 hexavalent-chromium maximum contaminant level for public water systems; no government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for any packaged-water form
read_across.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated, and the record says so on its face rather than asserting a maximum no government has written for this product form. No jurisdiction in the register sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for bottled water, packaged water or natural mineral water, and neither of the two textual packaged-water bridges this category relies on reaches the species: FDA 21 CFR 165.110(b)(4)(iii) incorporates the EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulation maximum contaminant levels and EPA sets no hexavalent-chromium MCL, and EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I carries no hexavalent-chromium parameter. The nearest applicable sovereign value is therefore the California State Water Resources Control Board Title 22 section 64431 Table 64431-A maximum contaminant level of 10 µg/L (0.01 mg/L, us_ca_swrcb_2024_cr-vi_chromium-hexavalent_mcl_10ugl), re-adopted in 2024 after health-risk and feasibility analysis, and it is carried across as a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS. Two hops are disclosed rather than argued around. not_material.rationale: Mercury in sealed packaged drinking water is present essentially as inorganic Hg(II). Methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury, so it is bounded by identity at the published total-mercury ceiling of 1 µg/L. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
not_material.reference_method: Methylmercury is not separately quantified as a routine cell. Total mercury is measured on every certification lot by cold-vapour atomic fluorescence or ICP-MS against the published total-mercury ceiling. Where a lot result reaches or exceeds half the total-mercury ceiling, speciation by GC-ICP-MS or HPLC-ICP-MS is run as a reflex and the source water is investigated; a detectable methyl fraction is an immediate non-conformance regardless of the total-mercury result.

not_material.rationale: Mercury in sealed packaged drinking water is present essentially as inorganic Hg(II). Methylation is a microbial process requiring anaerobic sulfate- or iron-reducing activity in sediment or biota; it does not occur in a treated, filtered, disinfected and sealed packaged-water matrix, and there is no aquatic food chain in the product to bioaccumulate methylmercury. Methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury, so it is bounded by identity at the published total-mercury ceiling of 1 µg/L. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
not_material.reference_method: Methylmercury is not separately quantified as a routine cell. Total mercury is measured on every certification lot by cold-vapour atomic fluorescence or ICP-MS against the published total-mercury ceiling. Where a lot result reaches or exceeds half the total-mercury ceiling, speciation by GC-ICP-MS or HPLC-ICP-MS is run as a reflex and the source water is investigated; a detectable methyl fraction is an immediate non-conformance regardless of the total-mercury result.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction in the register sets a methylmercury maximum for drinking water, bottled water or natural mineral water: of the 27 methylmercury rows in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, every one is a fish or aquatic-animal tissue limit and none is water-scoped. Every drinking-water and packaged-water instrument in the pool regulates mercury as total mercury with no methyl line, and Hong Kong Cap 132V regulates the packaged-drinking-water mercury cell as INORGANIC mercury (0.006 mg/kg, hk_cap132v_ihg_bottled-or-packaged-drinking-waters-other-than-natural_6), which is direct sovereign confirmation that the regulated mercury species in packaged water is the inorganic one. The only methylmercury maxima anywhere in the register are fish and aquatic-animal limits (for example fda_cpg540600_mehg_fish_1000), which govern a bioaccumulating tissue matrix and have no application to water.

Tin therefore remains a mandatory control cell; no number is invented.
control.reference_method: Tin by ICP-MS on the finished packaged product in its native per-litre as-consumed basis, on every certification lot, reported against the method limit of quantification rather than a ceiling. Where the product is presented in a tinplate or tin-coated container, the EU canned-beverage inorganic-tin maximum level recorded as the companion instrument applies as a regulatory hard stop in addition to this control.

Cr.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum (EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B end-state value)
Cr.basis_label: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)

This cell is published as a FIRM limit rather than as a screen, which is a deliberate departure from the HMTc default for total chromium and is compelled by the instruments themselves: in a food matrix total chromium is dominated by nutritionally benign Cr(III) and is a poor proxy for the health-relevant species, but the drinking-water instruments regulate total chromium precisely because the two species interconvert in aqueous media, and the Health Canada entry states in terms that the maximum acceptable concentration protects against chromium(VI) effects and is established for total chromium. read_across.label: disclosed read-across from the California SWRCB Title 22 s.64431 hexavalent-chromium maximum contaminant level for public water systems; no government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for any packaged-water form
read_across.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated, and the record says so on its face rather than asserting a maximum no government has written for this product form. Two hops are disclosed rather than argued around. The FDA and California nickel values descend from an EPA nickel MCL that was remanded in 1995, which is a further reason not to treat 100 µg/L as the operative ceiling when a current statutory value of 20 µg/L is applicable. CHILD-PROTECTIVE CHECK: EU Regulation 2024/1987 sets nickel at 100 µg/kg for liquid infant and young-child formula (eu2024_ni_formula_liquid_100), 250 µg/kg for non-soy powder and 400 µg/kg for soy-isolate powder; all are looser than the 20 µg/L value adopted here.

control.rationale: No sovereign sets a tin maximum for drinking water, bottled water or natural mineral water. The drinking-water instrument family carries no tin parameter at all (EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I Parts B and C; US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations; US FDA 21 CFR 165.110 standards of quality; Health Canada; NHMRC; WHO), and none of the national food-schedule packaged-water lines (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, India FSSAI 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013, Chile Decreto 977/1996, Fiji FSR 2009) carries a tin entry for water. A read-across is not supportable: the nearest sovereign tin maxima are the canned-food and canned-beverage maximum levels, which exist to bound dissolution of tin from a tinplate container wall into an acidic canned matrix, and the canned-beverage value (100 mg/kg inorganic tin) sits roughly four orders of magnitude above anything a packaged water can plausibly contain, so importing it would publish a ceiling that functions as no limit at all. The dominant packaging for this category (PET, HDPE, glass, aluminium) contains no tin. Nursery water is sold in PET or HDPE gallon and litre containers; there is no tinplate presentation of this form. Tin therefore remains a mandatory control cell; no number is invented.
control.reference_method: Tin by ICP-MS on the finished packaged product in its native per-litre as-consumed basis, on every certification lot, reported against the method limit of quantification rather than a ceiling. Any quantifiable tin result triggers investigation of the container, closure and liner, the filling line and the source water, and lot release is withheld pending root-cause identification and a clean re-test. Where the product is presented in a tinplate or tin-coated container, the EU canned-beverage inorganic-tin maximum level recorded as the companion instrument applies as a regulatory hard stop in addition to this control.

Al.label: strictest applicable sovereign value; stricter than every infant-specific instrument checked; an indicator / secondary / aesthetic parameter, disclosed as such
Al.basis_label: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Al.substantiation: Aluminium at 200 µg/L is the strictest applicable sovereign value and is disclosed here as a non-health-based parameter rather than a toxicological line: it is an Annex I Part C INDICATOR parameter in the EU Drinking Water Directive, a SECONDARY (aesthetically based) allowable level at FDA 21 CFR 165.110, and an AESTHETIC guideline for acid-soluble aluminium in the NHMRC guidelines. The health-based alternatives are far looser (Health Canada's maximum acceptable concentration of 2900 µg/L; California's MCL of 1000 µg/L), so adopting 200 µg/L is the strictest applicable treatment and is materially protective. Its aesthetic derivation is stated rather than concealed because the label of the parameter, not only its number, is part of the provenance. CHILD-PROTECTIVE CHECK: the only infant-specific aluminium maxima in the register are the FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19 values of 500 µg/kg for infant formula and follow-on formula (aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500) and 1000 µg/kg for soy-based infant formula (aunz_sch19_al_formula_soy_1000). Both are looser than the 200 µg/L packaged-water parameter adopted here, so the packaged-water value is itself the child-protective one. No infant instrument is adopted and no exposure or occurrence reasoning enters this cell.

Cr.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum; stricter than every infant-specific instrument checked
Cr.basis_label: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Cr.substantiation: Total chromium at 25 µg/L is the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B parametric value, the strictest applicable sovereign maximum; it is the Directive's end-state value, to be met by 12 January 2036, with a transitional value of 50 µg/L in force until then. The 50 µg/L tier (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Health Canada, WHO, California) and the 100 µg/L tier (EPA MCL, FDA 21 CFR 165.110) are named and not selected. This cell is published as a FIRM limit rather than as a screen, which is a deliberate departure from the HMTc default for total chromium and is compelled by the instruments themselves: in a food matrix total chromium is dominated by nutritionally benign Cr(III) and is a poor proxy for the health-relevant species, but the drinking-water instruments regulate total chromium precisely because the two species interconvert in aqueous media, and the Health Canada entry states in terms that the maximum acceptable concentration protects against chromium(VI) effects and is established for total chromium. The hexavalent species is not displaced: it is published separately at 10 µg/L. CHILD-PROTECTIVE CHECK: no jurisdiction sets a chromium maximum for infant formula, infant drinks or infant foods below the drinking-water value; the nearest infant-adjacent chromium instrument in the register is China's 2000 µg/kg for milk and modified milk powder (cn_crtotal_milk-powder-and-modified-milk-powder-gen_2000), eighty times looser than the 25 µg/L value adopted here.

read_across.label: disclosed read-across from the California SWRCB Title 22 s.64431 hexavalent-chromium maximum contaminant level for public water systems; no government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for any packaged-water form
read_across.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated, and the record says so on its face rather than asserting a maximum no government has written for this product form. No jurisdiction in the register sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for bottled water, packaged water or natural mineral water, and neither of the two textual packaged-water bridges this category relies on reaches the species: FDA 21 CFR 165.110(b)(4)(iii) incorporates the EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulation maximum contaminant levels and EPA sets no hexavalent-chromium MCL, and EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I carries no hexavalent-chromium parameter. The nearest applicable sovereign value is therefore the California State Water Resources Control Board Title 22 section 64431 Table 64431-A maximum contaminant level of 10 µg/L (0.01 mg/L, us_ca_swrcb_2024_cr-vi_chromium-hexavalent_mcl_10ugl), re-adopted in 2024 after health-risk and feasibility analysis, and it is carried across as a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS. Two hops are disclosed rather than argued around. First, SCOPE: the register records that instrument's product scope as 'public water systems in California', which is utility-delivered tap water and not a packaged good; HMTc has not identified, and does not cite, any California provision applying Title 22 section 64431 maximum contaminant levels to bottled water sold in the state, so this cell must not be read as an assertion that California enforces 10 µg/L against a packaged product. Second, SOVEREIGNTY: California is a sub-national government. The only alternative anywhere in the register is the NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines statement that hexavalent chromium should not exceed 50 µg/L (nhmrc2025_crvi_drinking_water_50), which is five times looser and carries the same drinking-water scope hop; it is named here and not selected because the method takes the strictest applicable value. The value is unchanged from the earlier compilation at 10 µg/L; only the provenance tag is corrected, from regulatory-alignment to read-across. HMTc publishes Cr-VI as its own cell in addition to total chromium: a hexavalent result never satisfies the total-chromium cell and a total-chromium result never satisfies this one, and the total-chromium cell on this row is a direct sovereign maximum for the product form that bounds this species from above. No infant-specific instrument checked sets a hexavalent-chromium value for water or for any other matrix, so this read-across is not displaced by an infant limit.

iAs.rationale: Published iAs of 6 ug/kg is retained as a precautionary program value after the instrument that carried it (il_fcs2016_ias_16_1_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_6) was superseded; the strictest in-force sovereign floor is 10 ug/kg (epa_mcl_ias_drinking_water_10). HMTc is a ratcheting program and does not loosen a live limit because an instrument died.
